dialogues.title: At a Language Exchange Event
dialogues.scene: Two people meet for the first time at a Korean language exchange and introduce themselves.

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ref: Hello! Nice to meet you (for the first time).

lines.speaker: 에밀리
lines.ref: Hello. I'm Emily.

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ref: I'm Minsu. What country are you from?

lines.speaker: 에밀리
lines.ref: I'm from the United States. I'm learning Korean now.

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ref: You speak Korean really well!

lines.speaker: 에밀리
lines.ref: Thank you. I can still only do a little.

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ref: What do you do (for work)?

lines.speaker: 에밀리
lines.ref: I'm a student. And you, Minsu?

lines.speaker: 민수
lines.ref: I'm an office worker. Nice to meet you.

lines.speaker: 에밀리
lines.ref: Nice to meet you too. I look forward to getting to know you.

vocab: 처음 뵙겠습니다 (nice to meet you, first time)
잘 부탁드려요 (I look forward to it)
dialogues.note: Koreans attach 씨 to a first or full name to be polite (민수 씨), but never to their own name. Asking someone's job and hometown early is normal small talk, not intrusive.

dialogues.title: Ordering at a Samgyeopsal Restaurant
dialogues.scene: A customer orders Korean barbecue and side dishes at a busy grill restaurant.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Excuse me, two servings of pork belly, please.

lines.speaker: 종업원
lines.ref: Sure, two servings of pork belly. And to drink?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.target: 콜라 하나하고 소주 한 병 주세요.
lines.ref: One cola and one bottle of soju, please.

lines.speaker: 종업원
lines.ref: Okay, got it. Please wait a moment.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Excuse me, could I have more side dishes?

lines.speaker: 종업원
lines.ref: Sure, I'll bring you more kimchi and lettuce.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Thank you. How do I eat this?

lines.speaker: 종업원
lines.ref: Wrap the meat and ssamjang in the lettuce and eat it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: It looks delicious! I'll pay later.

lines.speaker: 종업원
lines.ref: Okay, enjoy your meal.

dialogues.note: Side dishes (반찬) are free and refillable in Korea — just ask for 더 (more). Wrapping grilled meat in lettuce with garlic and ssamjang is called 쌈, a signature part of the meal.

dialogues.title: Asking for Directions in Seoul
dialogues.scene: A traveler asks a passerby how to reach the subway and Gyeongbokgung Palace.

lines.speaker: 여행자
lines.ref: Excuse me. Where is the subway station?

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.target: 이 길로 쭉 가면 오른쪽에 있어요.
lines.ref: If you go straight down this street, it's on the right.

lines.speaker: 여행자
lines.ref: Is it far from here?

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.ref: No, it takes about five minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: 여행자
lines.target: 경복궁에 가려면 몇 번 출구로 나가요?
lines.ref: To get to Gyeongbokgung, which exit should I take?

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.target: 오 번 출구로 나가세요. 바로 보여요.
lines.ref: Take exit five. You'll see it right away.

lines.speaker: 여행자
lines.ref: Is there also a convenience store nearby?

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.ref: Yes, there's one in front of the station.

lines.speaker: 여행자
lines.ref: Thank you so much. That was a big help.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.ref: Don't mention it. Have a good trip.

dialogues.note: Seoul subway exits are numbered, so locals give directions by exit number (몇 번 출구). Saying 별말씀을요 in reply to thanks is a warm, humble way to say 'you're welcome'.

dialogues.title: At a Korean Cosmetics Store
dialogues.scene: A shopper asks a clerk for skincare recommendations and checks the price.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Hello. I'm looking for skincare products.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.ref: What's your skin type?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: My skin is a bit dry.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.target: 그럼 이 수분 크림을 추천해 드려요.
lines.ref: Then I recommend this moisturizing cream.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Does this have a strong scent?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.ref: No, it's almost unscented. It's mild.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: That's nice. How much is this?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.target: 이만 오천 원이에요. 지금 세일 중이에요.
lines.ref: It's 25,000 won. It's on sale right now.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Then I'll take this one. Do you have samples too?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.target: 네, 샘플 몇 개 넣어 드릴게요.
lines.ref: Yes, I'll put in a few samples for you.

dialogues.note: Korean cosmetics shops almost always add free samples (샘플) with a purchase, and it's normal to ask for them. Prices are read with Sino-Korean numbers: 이만 오천 원 = 25,000 won.

dialogues.title: Booking a Cooking Class by Phone
dialogues.scene: A caller phones a studio to reserve a spot in a Korean cooking class.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Hello, I'd like to book a cooking class.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ref: Sure, which date would you like?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.target: 이번 주 토요일 오후에 자리가 있어요?
lines.ref: Is there a spot this Saturday afternoon?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.target: 토요일 두 시 반 수업에 자리가 있어요.
lines.ref: There's room in the 2:30 Saturday class.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Great. I'll book that class.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.target: 수업은 두 시간 정도 걸려요. 앞치마는 저희가 드려요.
lines.ref: The class takes about two hours. We provide the apron.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: What do I need to bring?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ref: You just need to come in comfortable clothes.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: How much is the class fee?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ref: It's 50,000 won, and ingredient costs are included.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Understood. See you on Saturday, then.

dialogues.note: Koreans answer the phone with 여보세요 (only on calls). The ending -는데요 softens a request and invites a response, which is why it's so common when booking or asking for something.

dialogues.title: At the Pharmacy
dialogues.scene: A customer describes cold symptoms and asks the pharmacist for medicine and instructions.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Hello. I've had a cold since yesterday.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.ref: What symptoms do you have?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: My throat hurts and my nose is running.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.ref: Do you have a fever too?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: A little. My head also hurts.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.ref: Then I'll give you this cold medicine.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: How many times a day should I take it?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.target: 식사 후에 하루 세 번 드세요.
lines.ref: Take it three times a day after meals.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: Could it make me drowsy?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.target: 네, 조금 졸릴 수 있으니 운전은 조심하세요.
lines.ref: Yes, it may make you a little drowsy, so be careful driving.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.ref: I understand. Thank you.

vocab: 콧물이 나다 (to have a runny nose)
dialogues.note: In Korea, pharmacists (약사) can dispense over-the-counter cold medicine directly without a prescription. Dosage is typically given as 하루 세 번 (three times a day), 식사 후 (after meals).
